episodes.202640: A shortwave moving across the area triggered thunderstorm development across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska the afternoon of July 6. Storms produced both strong winds and damaging hail with a brief landspout ground circulation reported.
episodes.202641: A shortwave moving across the area triggered thunderstorm development across southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska the afternoon of July 6. Storms produced both strong winds and damaging hail with a brief landspout ground circulation reported.
episodes.202669: Isolated severe thunderstorms over the Denver area and northeast Colorado plains. Video of a landspout tornado was taken by storm chasers. No damage was reported from the tornado or any other severe weather.
episodes.202681: Scattered showers and thunderstorms began to develop in an area with marginally sufficient shear and ample instability, ahead of a slow-moving cold front moving across central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours of July 7, 2025. Strong-to-severe thunderstorms continued across portions of Clinton County, where isolated instances of tree damage were observed.
episodes.202695: High based showers and thunderstorms produced wind gusts up to 66 mph (KAPA). A couple tree were up rooted in the Centennial area due to the strong winds. Lightning did not accompany all of the high wind reports.  As storms moved east into a more moist airmass, they began to produce hail. Including, a one inch hail was reported with a storm in Washington County.
episodes.202804: The monsoon high over northern Mexico built north into the desert southwest on July 6th and 7th. Daytime heating and moisture resulted in the development of scattered showers and storms across the northern and central mountains during the afternoon hours spreading east to lower elevations during the evening hours before tapering off shortly after sunset. Heavy rainfall from storms over the burn scars surrounding Ruidoso resulted in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars on July 6th followed by two separate rounds on July 7th with first round occurring during the early afternoon hours and the second round occurring during the mid evening hours just before sunset.
episodes.202853: Cheyenne County was on the northern edge of a more widespread severe weather event on July 7th. Thunderstorms produced large hail across the county.
episodes.203352: A low pressure system moved through the Great Lakes region, trailing a cold front that sparked showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.203588: After a few drier days, a stretch of active weather returned to the area beginning on July 7th. This was due to a cold front slowly approaching from the west while the remnants of a tropical system tracked north through the Carolinas and Virginia. While the bulk of precipitation associated with the tropical system stayed well east of the Appalachian Mountains, scattered showers and thunderstorms sprouted up in the lowlands of southeast Ohio ahead of the encroaching front and as a shortwave trough moved through. The front remained fairly stationary over the Ohio River on the 8th of July, then lifted back to the north as a disturbance moved over the Great Lakes region on the 9th. Warm, humid conditions fostered development of showers and thunderstorms each day, with lulls in activity during the overnight hours.||Total rainfall amounts between the 7th and 9th ranged from one to three inches across parts of southeast Ohio, with a pocket of around four inches that fell in Athens County. Heavy rain occurred rapidly and led to flash flooding on a few roads in Athens County on the 7th and in Meigs County on the 9th. In addition, damaging wind gusts embedded within these showers and storms, particularly on July 7th, resulted in downed trees across Athens and Morgan Counties.
episodes.203757: An isolated thunderstorm produced localized wind damage in central Virginia.
episodes.203888: Thunderstorms moving through the Detroit River and Lake St. Clair produced wind gusts up around 40 knots.
episodes.203889: A thunderstorm tracking through southern Lake Huron produced a wind gust around 35 knots.
episodes.204047: A crossing cold front with a weak shortwave passage spawned off clusters of thunderstorms in an environment characterized by DCAPE values >1000 J/kg with 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE and weak deep layer shear. Some storms turned severe and produced instances of damaging wind.
episodes.204070: A crossing cold front with a weak shortwave passage spawned off clusters of thunderstorms in an environment characterized by DCAPE values >1000 J/kg with 1500-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE and weak deep layer shear. Some storms turned severe and produced instances of damaging wind. In addition, an axis of high PWAT values near 2.0 resulted in flash flooding with slow moving storms.
episodes.204220: Weak vorticity maxima in the flow aloft and upslope flow encouraged shower and thunderstorm development in West Texas and Southeast New Mexico. One storm developed over Seminole, Texas and produced a microburst that caused damage to a metal building.
episodes.204259: Showers and thunderstorms initiated along and ahead of a quasi-stationary boundary during the afternoon of July 7th. The environment was characterized by high moisture and instability and weak shear, leading to gusty winds being the primary threat for the day. Thunderstorms overperformed, producing isolated wind damage and flash flooding.
episodes.204266: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado, and the southern Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon of July 7th. This activity moved east into the southeastern Nebraska Panhandle and southwestern Nebraska into the evening hours, producing ping pong ball sized hail over Garden County.
episodes.204322: Thunderstorms moved through Sheridan county with a storm generating an estimated wind gust nearing 60 mph.
episodes.204421: Thunderstorms developed across portions of the area during the afternoon hours of the 6th where golf ball to three inch diameter hail was reported in Norton county. Additional hail and wind reports were recorded in Rawlins, Thomas, Logan and Graham counties.
episodes.204469: Hot and humid conditions provided the fuel for storms triggered by a frontal system that swept across Central New York. Multiple storms became severe with damaging wind gusts. There were several reports of trees and wires down on roadways.
episodes.204471: A cluster of storms moved into northwest Kansas from eastern Colorado during the evening of the 6th.  These storms produced numerous reports of severe wind, with the strongest being a recorded 82 mph gust in eastern Sherman county.
episodes.204474: Storms developed during the late afternoon and led to hail in Haigler that ranged from pea size to golf ball size.
episodes.204475: A cluster of storms developed across eastern Colorado and led to severe wind gusts in Yuma, Cheyenne and Kit Carson counties with the strongest being 67 mph at the Burlington Airport (ITR).
episodes.204546: Thunderstorms developed across eastern Colorado during the afternoon of the 7th leading to hail and severe winds across Yuma county. Quarter size hail was reported around Yuma and wind gust of 77 mph was recorded at the Wray Airport.  Thunderstorm winds blew down many power poles in the northern part of Yuma County.
episodes.204580: Moist low level southeasterly flow with weak mid-level flow allowed slow moving thunderstorms with heavy rain to develop over far west Texas.  Locally heavy rain fell east of El Paso which brought flash flooding to areas east of Montana Vista.
episodes.204588: Low level southeast flow continued across areas east of the Rio Grande bringing in above average moisture to the El Paso area.  Weak mid-level flow kept storm motion slow and allowed for heavy rain to fall in northeast El Paso and produce flash flooding.
episodes.204671: Tropical Storm Chantal made landfall over northeastern South Carolina during the morning hours of July 6. The remnants of Chantal then tracked west-northwest into portions of central North Carolina, stalling out over the area before tracking east-northeast into Virginia by the 7th of July. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred from record rainfall of up to 11 inches in some spots of the Piedmont, included 6 flash flood fatalities across Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Widespread flooding particularly affected the counties of Orange, Chatman, and Moore. Four EF-1 tornadoes also touched down over portions Lee, Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Preliminary loss estimates across central North Carolina exceeded 40 million.
episodes.205001: On July 7, 2025, a lee surface trough pushed into western Nebraska and South Dakota during the afternoon, initiating scattered thunderstorms across the region. By evening, these storms consolidated into a larger mesoscale convective system (MCS) that tracked into northeast Nebraska before expanding southward across eastern Nebraska and southwest Iowa through the night.||Ahead of the main MCS, several discrete supercells developed in northeast Nebraska, producing significant hail. Notable reports included measured 3-inch diameter stones 3 miles west of Obert, NE; hail estimated near tennis-ball size 4 miles west-northwest of Winnetoon, NE; and a measured 1.75-inch stone 3 miles east-southeast of Wynot, NE. As the evening progressed, these initial cells were absorbed into the growing MCS, which transitioned into a primarily damaging wind threat. A swath of measured wind gusts ranging from 58 to 67 mph was reported across much of east-central Nebraska into southwest Iowa.||The convective complex gradually weakened as it approached the northern Kansas and Missouri border. However, widespread heavy rainfall persisted behind the system, leading to flooding concerns���particularly in northeast Nebraska, where emergency management reported water over multiple highways and roadways in Antelope, Boone, and Platte Counties.
episodes.205179: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of eastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon and evening of the 7th. Very unstable air combined with very weak wind shear supported intense, relatively short-lived, thunderstorm development, the strongest of which produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.205219: Heavy rainfall and isolated strong storms impacted portions of southeast Arkansas.
episodes.205250: Severe thunderstorms including supercells produced large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes across parts of eastern North Dakota.
episodes.205252: Severe thunderstorms including supercells produced large hail, damaging winds and tornadoes across parts of eastern North Dakota and west central Minnesota.
episodes.205429: With a moist airmass in place over the region, afternoon pulse thunderstorms developed across southwestern Missouri producing localized wind damage and flooding. Significant flooding occurred in eastern Greene County where between 3 and 6 inches of rain fall over a less than 6 hour period as persistent slow moving storms developed over the county. During the period, some locations saw in excess of an inch of rain in a 15 minute period.
episodes.205533: Isolated thunderstorms developed across portions of south-central and southeast Kansas during the early afternoon hours of July 6th. Thunderstorm coverage became more-numerous during the mid to late afternoon hours across south-central Kansas. These particular storms produced severe caliber hail and damaging winds.
episodes.205539: Late morning convection within deep layer southwest flow over the state south of the remnants of Tropical Depression Chantal centered over southeastern Virginia produces a waterspout offshore Clearwater Beach in Pinellas County.
episodes.205558: A west to east line of thunderstorms moving southward through Southeast Missouri produced heavy rainfall during the afternoon of the 7th. Very high precipitable water values near 2.0 helped fuel the downpours, which produced ponding of water in Poplar Bluff.
episodes.205611: Thunderstorms fired along a convergence zone pushing southeast across southeast South Dakota during the afternoon, with instability as high as 1500-2500 J/kg and modest effective shear of 25 to 35 knots.  While storm shear and cold pool dynamics remained balanced, isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts gradually transitioned to the latter before weakening during the mid-evening hours.
episodes.205632: Cold front moved into Maine from the northwest. Warm sector ahead of aforementioned cold front, along with plenty of moisture, led to a warm, humid day, along with plentiful instability, that resulted in convection in Piscataquis and Penobscot counties. Storm originally developed in Quebec / western Maine, and began to strengthen in Piscataquis county. Storms eventually weakened and continued to move east into New Brunswick. Caused some wind damage along Telos Road in Piscataquis, knocking down 4 healthy trees. Some more thunderstorms developed in southern Penobscot, later in the afternoon, resulting in knocked trees and various lightning strikes. These storms eventually weakened and moved offshore.
episodes.205687: From the July 4th weekend into the early part of the following week, a weak upper trough lingered over North and Central Texas, triggering several days of scattered showers and thunderstorms. A saturated atmosphere combined with slow storm motions resulted in numerous flash flooding events throughout the region, particularly in Central Texas.
episodes.205788: Low pressure, Post-Tropical Cyclone Chantal, induced heavy rain and flash flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.205888: Isolated strong thunderstorms moved across northeast South Dakota during the afternoon, producing large hail.
episodes.205904: Showers and thunderstorms developed along lake breeze boundaries and a passing cold front on the afternoon of July 7. While there was plenty of instability, shear values were lower, but just enough to support a few severe thunderstorms that produced damage along with a tornado.
episodes.205940: A few thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening and produced minor wind damage and quarter size hail reports.
episodes.205980: A few thunderstorms during the afternoon hours produced marginal severe weather across the area.
episodes.206035: During the overnight to early morning hours of July 7th, a small upper level system helped produce a cluster of strong to severe storms straddling the Texas-Oklahoma state line. A power pole and several large tree branches were snapped in Wheeler, TX as a result, with another severe gust occurring further south in Clarendon. While this was ongoing, another line of storms entered the Oklahoma Panhandle from Kansas, generating a 64 mph wind gust in Hooker, OK.
episodes.206036: During the overnight to early morning hours of July 7th, a small upper level system helped produce a cluster of strong to severe storms straddling the Texas-Oklahoma state line. A power pole and several large tree branches were snapped in Wheeler, TX as a result, with another severe gust occurring further south in Clarendon. While this was ongoing, another line of storms entered the Oklahoma Panhandle from Kansas, generating a 64 mph wind gust in Hooker, OK.
episodes.206119: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours inland of the sea breeze across portions of southeast South Carolina. These storms produced gusty winds and frequent cloud to ground lightning.
episodes.206130: Remnant tropical moisture along with an upper level area of low pressure resulted in showers and thunderstorms across portions of the northwest Hill Country, which produced flash flooding on July 7th. Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of the Concho Valley and Big Country on July 8th and July 9th, producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.206190: Heavy rainfall associated with slow-moving thunderstorms on July 7, 2025, produced flash flooding in portions of Orleans Parish. Social media photos showed water over a foot deep along General Meyer Avenue near Shirley Drive in New Orleans.
episodes.206306: Two supercells that developed along the higher terrain pushed across El Paso County due to westerly flow aloft. Both supercells would go on to produce swaths of severe hail across central El Paso County.
episodes.206321: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced a strong wind gust along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.206362: Outflow gust from a nearby thunderstorm affected the Rock Springs Airport.
episodes.206437: A line of thunderstorms associated with a surface cold front dropped into the northern reaches of New Hampshire on the evening of July 6th.  Most storms just brought gusty winds and downpours, but isolated tree damage did occur.
episodes.206729: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms produced occasionally severe wind gusts across parts of Mississippi.
episodes.207831: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward across northern and central OH during the afternoon through early evening of July 7th as a weak low along the front drifted generally eastward in vicinity of northeastern Lake Ontario. Along and ahead of the front, thunderstorms in the form of scattered multicells and a few supercells developed and persisted generally eastward across NE OH, in the warm and humid sector. One of the supercells produced a weak tornado in Medina County, while the descending rear-inflow jet of a bow echo produced minor and isolated straight-line wind damage in Trumbull County. These storms occurred amidst moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively.

Damage continued east-southeast|to the north of County Road 23 with dozens of hardwood trees |snapped on the north side of a large farm area.
